subject: Urgent: Checkout p95 latency surge — request fallback + rollback authorization
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@stellarpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Checkout API latency spike (p95) — urgent

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp jump in Checkout API latency this morning across three regions. p95 for tokenized checkout is up from ~180ms to ~1.4s and several timeouts have bubbled up to our customers' error dashboards. This began around 08:30 PT.

Can you confirm whether the recent model rollout (model-6b-v3-quant) was applied to our dedicated pool? Our engineering ops team saw an increased rate of model queueing on the 6b-v3 nodes. We need a fallback plan — if we can temporarily route Checkout calls to the prior variant (model-6b-v2) or enable the MFF fallback for 30–60 minutes that would reduce customer impact.

We can provide logs and a p95 dump — attached is a short perf snapshot (perf_dump_1128.json). Please advise next steps; we may escalate to legal/exec if this impacts SLAs.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Carter
Site Reliability Lead, StellarPay

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout API latency spike (p95) — urgent

Emily — thanks for the heads up and the perf snapshot. I'm escalating internally now.

Short answer: yes — your Dedicated pool received the model-6b-v3-quant variant as a staged rollout at 02:00 PT. We have rollback and variant-fallback controls available, but because this is a Dedicated customer with pinned model policies we need a written authorization to perform a controlled rollback/variant swap that could briefly affect token accounting.

Proposed immediate mitigation (if you authorize):
- Canary traffic shift: divert 10% of Checkout traffic to model-6b-v2 in region us-west for 30 minutes to validate p95 improvement.
- If p95 improves >= 40% and error rate drops, escalate to 100% rollback for the next 60 minutes and monitor.
- Post-rollback: collect traces for a regression triage and file a formal incident report.

We also can enable an automatic KV prefix cache prewarm for Checkout endpoints to reduce tail latency within ~10 mins. That doesn't require rollback authorization but is not guaranteed to eliminate the spike.

Request from Redwood legal/ops: please confirm authorization for a temporary variant rollback (model-6b-v3-quant -> model-6b-v2) for up to 90 minutes. If you approve, reply with OK AUTHORIZE ROLLBACK and we will proceed and send a brief pre/post summary.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout API latency spike (p95) — urgent

Soojin — on call now with runtime and infra. Quick notes:
- Telemetry confirms increased scheduling latency on nodes with model-6b-v3-quant under longer sequence workloads (checkout session tokenization with metadata).
- There is a known kernel path regression in 6b-v3-quant when sequence length > 1024 with this quant profile; runtime can route to the 6b-v2 kernel path with minimal perf tradeoffs.

Action we need from CS: signed rollback authorization for Dedicated pools. Engineering can perform a controlled canary swap and metricized rollback with automatic fallback to v3 after 2 hours if no regression found.

I authorize the canary plan from infra — but we need billing/contract sign-off for SLA exception (customer-impact window) and legal to sign off on a temporary configuration change that deviates from pinned versions.

Marissa/Rishi — can you approve the SLA exception and confirm if we should use a locked rollback (no auto-reapply) or a temporary override (auto-reapply after 2h)? Recommend temporary override disabled (i.e., manual re-enable) to allow triage.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Runtime

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout API latency spike (p95) — urgent

Emily — thanks, and thanks for the perf dump. We are prepared to run the canary as soon as we receive explicit authorization. For clarity, the canary plan is:
- 10:00 PT today: route 10% Checkout traffic in us-west to model-6b-v2 for 30 minutes.
- If p95 drops by >= 40% and error rate drops to baseline, escalate to full rollback for 60 minutes.
- We will collect detailed traces and send a post-action incident summary within 3 hours.

To proceed we need: ONE LINE AUTH: "OK AUTHORIZE ROLLBACK" from your security or product owner. If you prefer Redwood to perform a temporary override (no auto-reapply), say "MANUAL REVERT"; if you prefer Redwood to auto-reapply v3 after 2 hours, say "AUTO REAPPLY 2H".

Also attaching the perf snapshot you provided to our incident ticket and adding the related HubSpot record HS-42819 for your account.

If you do not want any rollback, we can attempt cache prewarm and request-hinting but that may not fully remove p95 tail for longer sequences.

— Soojin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout API latency spike (p95) — urgent

All — I approve an exception for the StellarPay Dedicated pool. Decision: MANUAL REVERT (no auto-reapply).

I've attached the signed rollback authorization form (rollback_auth_form.pdf) to this thread and recorded the SLA exception in our internal tracker (HS-42819). Please proceed with the canary and follow the metric gates defined by Soojin. Engineering: coordinate the swap window with ops and notify the customer-facing docket.

On a related note: after rollback, schedule a short regression triage meeting (30 min) with runtime and research to decide whether we should backport the kernel fix or modify quant profiles for 6b-v3.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
